scope.summary: Implement StudioConstraint (hsk.studio.constraint@1) governing how a non-auto-layout child responds when its parent frame resizes: exactly one horizontal constraint (left, right, left-and-right stretch, center, scale) and one vertical constraint (top, bottom, top-and-bottom stretch, center, scale), default top-left; the scale constraint stores size/position as percentages of the parent for proportional growth; and temporarily suspending child constraints during a modifier-held parent-resize drag. Unify resizing: a child is governed by StudioAutoLayout when the parent is an auto-layout frame and by StudioConstraint otherwise; the two MUST NOT both drive the same child on the same axis, and absolute-positioned auto-layout children fall back to StudioConstraint. The constraint panel is an operator surface.

spec_clauses.spec_clause_text: [STU-DS-046] `StudioConstraint` (schema id `hsk.studio.constraint@1`) governs how a non-auto-layout child responds when its parent frame resizes.
[STU-DS-046a] Each child MUST carry exactly one horizontal constraint — left, right, left-and-right (stretch), center, or scale — controlling its x position and width on parent resize.

[STU-DS-046b] Each child MUST carry exactly one vertical constraint — top, bottom, top-and-bottom (stretch), center, or scale — controlling its y position and height on parent resize. The default constraint is top-left.
[STU-DS-046c] The scale constraint MUST store size and position as percentages of the parent so the child grows and shrinks proportionally on both axes.

[STU-DS-046d] Studio MUST support temporarily suspending child constraints during a parent resize (modifier-held drag) so the frame resizes without repositioning children. ### 10. Layout Grids (StudioLayoutGrid)

[STU-DS-048] Resizing behavior across the layout system is unified: a child's response to a resizing parent is governed by `StudioAutoLayout` participation ([STU-DS-042]) when the parent is an auto-layout frame, and by `StudioConstraint` ([STU-DS-046]) otherwise. The two MUST NOT both drive the same child on the same axis simultaneously; absolute-positioned auto-layout children ([STU-DS-044]) fall back to `StudioConstraint`. ### 11. Design-System Analytics and Library-Management Posture This group fixes the operational posture of the whole design system: it is local-first authority, works offline, and treats any cloud aggregation as an optional adapter rather than a dependency.

scope.summary: Implement StudioConstraint (hsk.studio.constraint@1) governing how a non-auto-layout child responds when its parent frame resizes: exactly one horizontal constraint (left, right, left-and-right stretch, center, scale) and one vertical constraint (top, bottom, top-and-bottom stretch, center, scale), default top-left; the scale constraint stores size/position as percentages of the parent for proportional growth; and temporarily suspending child constraints during a modifier-held parent-resize drag. Unify resizing: a child is governed by StudioAutoLayout when the parent is an auto-layout frame and by StudioConstraint otherwise; the two MUST NOT both drive the same child on the same axis, and absolute-positioned auto-layout children fall back to StudioConstraint. The constraint panel is an operator surface.

spec_clauses.spec_clause_text: [STU-DS-046] `StudioConstraint` (schema id `hsk.studio.constraint@1`) governs how a non-auto-layout child responds when its parent frame resizes.
[STU-DS-046a] Each child MUST carry exactly one horizontal constraint — left, right, left-and-right (stretch), center, or scale — controlling its x position and width on parent resize.

[STU-DS-046b] Each child MUST carry exactly one vertical constraint — top, bottom, top-and-bottom (stretch), center, or scale — controlling its y position and height on parent resize. The default constraint is top-left.
[STU-DS-046c] The scale constraint MUST store size and position as percentages of the parent so the child grows and shrinks proportionally on both axes.

[STU-DS-046d] Studio MUST support temporarily suspending child constraints during a parent resize (modifier-held drag) so the frame resizes without repositioning children. ### 10. Layout Grids (StudioLayoutGrid)

[STU-DS-048] Resizing behavior across the layout system is unified: a child's response to a resizing parent is governed by `StudioAutoLayout` participation ([STU-DS-042]) when the parent is an auto-layout frame, and by `StudioConstraint` ([STU-DS-046]) otherwise. The two MUST NOT both drive the same child on the same axis simultaneously; absolute-positioned auto-layout children ([STU-DS-044]) fall back to `StudioConstraint`. ### 11. Design-System Analytics and Library-Management Posture This group fixes the operational posture of the whole design system: it is local-first authority, works offline, and treats any cloud aggregation as an optional adapter rather than a dependency.

original_scope.summary: Implement StudioConstraint (hsk.studio.constraint@1) governing how a non-auto-layout child responds when its parent frame resizes: exactly one horizontal constraint (left, right, left-and-right stretch, center, scale) and one vertical constraint (top, bottom, top-and-bottom stretch, center, scale), default top-left; the scale constraint stores size/position as percentages of the parent for proportional growth; and temporarily suspending child constraints during a modifier-held parent-resize drag. Unify resizing: a child is governed by StudioAutoLayout when the parent is an auto-layout frame and by StudioConstraint otherwise; the two MUST NOT both drive the same child on the same axis, and absolute-positioned auto-layout children fall back to StudioConstraint. The constraint panel is an operator surface.
